posts.title: Build a rotating feed of web projects
posts.promise: Collect forum picks on a schedule and publish a browsable, ranked discovery feed.
posts.whatItIs: Deploylist is a website for discovering standalone web projects selected from Hacker News and Reddit. Its maker says it ingests submissions automatically every three days, ranks projects using upvotes from the previous week and month, and leaves sites with embedding problems on the leaderboard while excluding them from the live view. A small student version could follow a few public communities and display selected links with their source and score. This is a curation loop, not a promise that a ranking identifies the best projects.
posts.whoPays: Hypothesis: readers seeking new web projects, or sponsors wanting to reach them, might pay for a focused discovery feed; the source establishes no customers, sponsorships, or revenue.
loop: Choose public forums and define which submissions count as standalone projects.
On a schedule, collect eligible posts and their visible vote counts.
Filter out projects hosted on excluded major platforms.
Rank entries using recent and monthly forum votes.
Check whether each project can be embedded and show eligible entries in a feed.
Review ranking and broken or misleading entries, then adjust rules.
posts.evidence: In a Show HN post, the maker says Deploylist automatically ingests every three days and selects highly upvoted posts from linked subreddits and Hacker News over weekly and monthly windows. The maker says projects with embedding issues stay ranked but are omitted from the live view. This is a founder description, not independent evidence of reliability, audience, or revenue.
posts.uncertainty: The source does not establish readership, customer demand, or earnings. Votes are an imperfect quality signal, and source rules or embed availability can change. A student version should use a small set of public forums, respect their access rules, and have a person review exclusions and featured projects. The automated part is collecting, filtering, ranking, and refreshing the feed; editorial choices and disputed entries need human oversight.
first24Hours: Select two public forums and write down allowed access methods and inclusion rules.
Manually collect a small set of eligible project links with their vote counts and dates.
Build a simple page that ranks those records and lets a person flag excluded or broken entries.
